Package frc.lib.NinjasLib.util

Class DerivativeCalculator

java.lang.Object
frc.lib.NinjasLib.util.DerivativeCalculator
public class DerivativeCalculator extends Object
Computes a smoothed time-derivative (rate of change) of a scalar value sampled over time, e.g. to estimate velocity from repeated position measurements. This is stateful: each call to calculate(double) uses the value and timestamp from the previous call, so it must be called once per sample (typically once per periodic loop) with a consistent time source, and a single instance should not be shared across unrelated signals.

  • Method Details

    • calculate

      public double calculate(double currentValue)
      Feeds in a new sample and returns the current smoothed derivative estimate. The first call after construction (or after reset()) has no prior sample to compare against, so it returns 0.0 and only records currentValue as the baseline for the next call.
      Parameters:
      currentValue - The latest sampled value.
      Returns:
      The smoothed rate of change of the value, per second.

    • get

      public double get()
      Returns:
      The most recently computed derivative, without taking a new sample. Same value calculate(double) last returned.

    • reset

      public void reset()
      Clears all accumulated state (the moving-average filter and the last sample), so the next call to calculate(double) behaves as if this were a freshly constructed calculator.
